correctness.rationale: For every n>=4, the primary facet theorem yields precisely the n(n+1)/2 interval support inequalities. The projected Euclidean normal length is sqrt(q(D-q)/D). A double-cover of all coordinate variables by end-singleton and adjacent-pair normals gives the sharp upper bound. An explicit baseline center attains it, by strict concavity of the normal-length function. Equalities in the sharp bound force the linear slack parametrization; tight triples fix the boundary slacks and upper-bound the independent middle slacks. Every larger interval is checked by a decreasing-difference sum, establishing an exact cube of dimension n-4, with no omitted centers. The bundled checker independently solves 8 intrinsic Chebyshev LPs, evaluates 137 box-corner instances and checks 110 facet ranks. Finite experiments supplement, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The path is a canonical family in the theory of cosmological polytopes, previously analyzed via faces, recursive f-vectors and triangulations. The new result extracts an intrinsic, non-affine-invariant metric property and a structurally complete classification of all optimal centers. The linear growth of the cubical center dimension and exact onset of nonuniqueness at n=5 are not captured by prior volume or combinatorial statements; the two-cover facet certificate and interval-concavity mechanism provide independently useful geometric structure.
